title: AI Benchmark Oracle And Eval Foundation
goal: Use AI where it provides the most value for AegisPT quality: comparing benchmark-run output against known expected vulnerability families and explaining coverage gaps without changing execution or canonical findings.
scope: Implement an optional AI-assisted benchmark-evaluation layer for lab and validation runs only. The layer should consume structured benchmark metadata, expected-finding catalogs, and actual run output, then produce an advisory expected-vs-actual report with: benchmark family coverage, likely misses, likely false positives, possible root-cause explanations, and confidence/grounding metadata. Use reference-guided grading rather than open-ended opinion, keep the output review-only, and store the result separately from canonical findings and release gates. Integrate with existing AI provider boundaries and the future deterministic validation matrix from backlog-99 where possible, but do not replace deterministic scoring with AI judgment.
generation_reason: Operator feedback highlighted that AI should have helped compare the Gruyere run against what the site is actually known to contain. OpenAI evaluation guidance also recommends task-specific, reference-guided evals, which fits benchmark grading far better than using AI as a generic scanner.

constraints.active_task_gate: Do not implement this task until it is the single active task in NEXT_TASK.md.
constraints.scope_creep_guard: Benchmark-evaluation only. No scan dispatch, no finding creation, no scope expansion, no canonical pass/fail release authority, and no customer-target overreach.
notes: Use reference-guided grading and grounding metadata, not open-ended AI verdicts.
Outputs must remain advisory and separate from canonical findings.
Provider-disabled and provider-failure states must remain truthful.

success_criteria: An optional AI-assisted benchmark gap report can be generated for benchmark runs.
The report clearly distinguishes found, missed, uncertain, and unexpected signals.
Grounding metadata ties conclusions back to benchmark metadata and actual run artifacts.
Provider-disabled and provider-failure paths produce truthful fallback behavior.
Tests cover reference-guided grading input, sparse artifact cases, disabled provider, and advisory-only boundaries.
AI output does not create findings, change release gates, or dispatch work.
must_not_touch: pack registry, validation, approval, deployment, or runtime binding flows

acceptance_criteria: AI benchmark report is advisory-only and reference-guided.
Provider failure does not affect canonical benchmark results.

before_promotion: The prior active task is completed and logged.
Deterministic benchmark metadata exists or the task is narrowed to report-only plumbing.
after_completion: Update DONE_LOG.md with AI benchmark-eval implementation and validation evidence.
Update CURRENT_STATE.md with AI benchmark-oracle boundaries and current status.
Promote exactly one next approved task package into NEXT_TASK.md, or set an explicit holding state if the queue is exhausted.
